inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.
inputs.original_proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: Channel count validation removed for poll case - the check changed from (sched_mode || params.poll_pid != 0) to just sched_mode, removing validation when poll_pid is set but sched.count is 0; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: if (sched_mode && t->chan_count == 0)
questions: What is the intended behavior when both sched_mode and poll_pid are active? The original code prevented both from being true simultaneously.
Is channel 0 always the correct channel for single-PID polling, or should a channel be selected based on the PID?
Does providing a filter (rx_id) guarantee that chan_count > 0, or can resolve_channels return zero channels even with a filter?

claim: Unsafe array access without bounds checking - chans[0] accessed without validating chan_count > 0; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);
nits: The comment in SettingsPage.qml states '?poll= is ignored under the obd2 default' but the code actively uses poll_pid to build requests
The 6-byte buffer for req may be insufficient for CAN FD frames which can be 64+ bytes
Consider adding an assertion or explicit bounds check before accessing chans[0]
